title: fix(sdk): keep cancellation active while reading response bodies
author: ale-rls
pr_body_excerpt:
Fixes #16138

- Keeps SDK cancellation and timeout protection active while non-stream response bodies are consumed, so cancelled JSON/binary downloads reject instead of completing.
- Preserves CANCELLED/499 and TIMEOUT/408, including delayed HTTP-error bodies. Successful streams retain their existing header-only timeout and reader cancellation.
- Migrates existing private-helper callers without changing public signatures, dependencies, or secondary image-download lifecycles.
- Verification: eight real HTTP regressions fail before the fix and pass after it; all 107 SDK tests, typecheck, ESM/CJS/browser/declaration builds, Biome and independent built-SDK loopback checks pass. Zero generation calls or Pollen spent.

gist.headline: The stop button means stop
gist.blurb: The SDK keeps an eye on the clock while reading response bodies. Cancelled downloads stop instead of quietly finishing the job.
gist.summary: The SDK keeps cancellation and timeout protection active while consuming non-stream JSON and binary response bodies, preserving CANCELLED/499 and TIMEOUT/408 even when HTTP-error bodies arrive late.
gist.impact: SDK calls cancelled or timed out during a non-stream body download reject with the appropriate error; successful streams keep their existing header-only timeout behavior.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy pixel workbench represents an SDK response arriving in pieces: a CRT robot carries JSON and binary parcels along a little vine-lined path while Polli uses a tiny stop button and clock to halt a parcel mid-delivery. The stopped parcel makes cancellation during body reading visible without suggesting a change to streaming.
